svg.aria-label: The difference between an assistant and an agent is whether it writes anything. An assistant only reads: it states opening hours, gives the address and directions, quotes a published price, answers a question from your knowledge base, and takes a message for someone to act on later. An agent writes: it checks a live calendar and holds the slot, creates the record in your system with the fields filled in, sends the confirmation text, pages the on-call person and confirms they picked up, and warm-transfers a caller mid-conversation. The right-hand column is where the labour saving lives, and it is the column a demo call almost never shows.
svg.text: Assistant or agent? Ask what it writes
Both columns sound identical on a call. Only one of them takes work off a person’s desk.

g.text: Quotes a price off the published list

svg.text: Somebody still opens the message in the morning and
does the actual work. The call was captured, not handled.

g.text: Reads a live calendar and holds the slot
Creates the record, fields already filled
Pages on-call and checks somebody woke

svg.text: Every line here needs a credential, a permission and a
rule for what happens when the write fails.
The question that separates vendors: “in the demo I just heard, which of those right-hand rows actually happened in a real system?”
